To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) RGB stereo can be used as an efficient, accurate and robust input to the problem of hand and hand-object interaction 3D tracking; 2) the proposed stereo-based approach outperforms state of the art methods for RGBD-based hand tracking; 3) the method can be used to solve the problem in real time, even for two interacting hands.
1) 3D hand and hand-object tracking can be performed in real time using only two cameras, and 2) stereo-based tracking performs equally well, if not better, to its RGBD counterparts.

1) accurate and efficient 6-DOF tracking of hands and hand-object interactions is possible using short-baseline stereo; 2) stereo-based 3D reconstruction is not required for this purpose; and 3) stereo-based 6-DOFs hand tracking is as good as, or even better than, RGBD-based 3D tracking, in terms of accuracy, and much faster.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a fundamental question: is 3D hand motion tracking based on RGB stereo as accurate and efficient as tracking based on RGBD cameras?
the problem of 2D to 3D hand pose estimation from RGB stereo images.
the problem of 6D tracking of hands and hand-object interactions using only a pair of synchronized RGB cameras.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our approach can be seen as an alternative to the RGBD-based methods for the 3D tracking problem, and it has the advantage of being applicable to RGB stereo cameras.
our method is the first to show that 3D hand and hand-object tracking is feasible using RGB stereo.
the proposed method provides an efficient and accurate alternative to existing RGBD-based approaches for the task of 3D hand and hand-object tracking.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is now possible to perform 3D hand and hand-object tracking in real-time using commodity RGB stereo cameras.
, by using stereo, we are able to track hands with the accuracy and robustness of RGBD cameras, but with significantly less computational complexity.
, by using stereo cameras and the proposed algorithm, we can track hands with a level of accuracy comparable to that of RGBD cameras, at a fraction of the cost.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RGB-based stereo is a valid alternative to RGBD-based approaches, especially when depth information is unavailable, as is the case in the vast majority of video games.
RGB-based 3D tracking methods, even for the difficult task of hand tracking, can be competitive to RGBD-based approaches.
RGB stereo cameras are capable of producing high quality 3D hand data, and this can be done efficiently.
